regex-vis — every edit-panel under test

R1 · simple-string content

Click the literal "a" to open the simple-string panel.

R2 · class-character content

Click "\d" / "\w" / "\s" to open the class-character panel.

R3 · ranges content

Click "[a-z0-9]" to open the ranges panel.

R4 · negated ranges content

Click "[^a-z]" — same panel as R3 with negate flag toggled.

R5 · back-reference content

Click the "\\1" to open the back-ref panel.

R6 · word-boundary assertion

Click "\b" to open the word-boundary panel.

R7 · beginning anchor

Click "^" to open the beginning-assertion panel.

R8 · end anchor

Click "$" to open the end-assertion panel.

R9 · capturing group

Click the rounded outer group to open the group panel.

R10 · named capturing group

Click the named group to open the group panel with name field.

R11 · non-capturing group

Click "(?:…)" to open the group panel with non-capturing kind.

R12 · lookahead

Click "(?=…)" to open the look-around panel.

R13 · negative lookahead

Click "(?!…)" — same panel, negate=true.

R14 · lookbehind

Click "(?<=…)" to open the look-around panel.

R15 · negative lookbehind

Click "(?<!…)" — same panel, negate=true.

R16 · quantifier (one-or-more)

Click the "a+" to open content + quantifier panels.

R17 · quantifier (custom range)

Click "a{2,5}" to verify min/max inputs in quantifier panel.

R18 · lazy quantifier

Click "a+?" — quantifier panel with lazy flag.

R19 · alternation

Choice/alternation has no dedicated panel; clicking selects sub-tree.

R20 · stress — complex nested email-ish

Deep nested combination — many controls, panels should still resolve.

R21 · stress — ISO date

Multiple alternations inside groups.

R22 · stress — kitchen sink

Lookarounds + back-ref + named + boundary + quantifier in one regex.
